claim: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding charges roughly CNY 55-60 for an adult ticket, with under-6 and over-60 free, bookable up to 14 days in advance via WeChat or authorized platforms (Trip.com, Meituan).
quote: A standard adult ticket is usually around RMB 55-60. Children under 6 are free of charge. Visitors over 60 are free of charge. Tickets are available for reservation 14 days in advance.

claim: The Chengdu Panda Base opens 7:30 (Mar-Oct) / 8:00 (Nov-Feb) and pandas are most active in the early morning, so visitors should arrive by 7:15-7:30 AM to beat crowds and see active pandas during feeding.
quote: The best time is early morning, ideally from 7:30 AM to around 9:30 AM. That is when pandas are most active and the crowds are still manageable. Aim to arrive by 7:15-7:30 AM.

claim: A classic Chengdu history-and-culture day pairs Wuhou Shrine (Three Kingdoms), the adjacent Jinli Street, and Du Fu Thatched Cottage, with the Panda Base as the standout half-day excursion.
quote: A recommended two-day history and culture line includes visiting Wuhou Shrine for Three Kingdoms culture, Du Fu Thatched Cottage for its tranquil gardens and Tang poetry charm, and Jinsha Site Museum.

claim: The Jinsha Site Museum is fully closed from Dec 5, 2025 to April 30, 2027 for its first major upgrade since 2007, so it is unavailable to weekend visitors in June 2026.
quote: The Jinsha Site Museum in Chengdu, Sichuan province, will close from Dec 5, 2025 to April 30, 2027 for its first major upgrade since its opening in 2007. All areas including the relic hall and exhibition hall will be closed to the public.

claim: Wuhou Shrine (dedicated to Three Kingdoms strategist Zhuge Liang) costs about CNY 50 (CNY 25 half-price), opens 9:00-18:00 with ticket sales ending at 17:00, and adjoins the photogenic Jinli ancient street.
quote: Tickets are CNY 50, half-price tickets are CNY 25. Opening hours: 9:00-18:00 (ticket sales stop at 17:00).

claim: Du Fu Thatched Cottage, the former Chengdu residence of Tang poet Du Fu, is a tranquil garden-museum costing around CNY 50 and typically needs 1.5-2 hours.
quote: Du Fu Thatched Cottage is the former Chengdu residence of the famous Tang Dynasty poet Du Fu, who lived here for nearly four years and created hundreds of poems during his stay.

claim: Chengdu Museum at Tianfu Square is free (online real-name reservation required), open Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00 with extended Fri-Sat hours to 20:30, and holds 200,000+ relics including an 8.5-ton Warring States stone rhinoceros.
quote: General admission is free (with required online reservation). Weekdays 09:00-17:00; Weekends 09:00-20:30. The museum houses over 200,000 cultural relics.

claim: Dujiangyan panda volunteer programs (open to ages 8-70, full-day, making panda food and watching feeding) are a deeper alternative to the Chengdu base, but the Dujiangyan base is closed from April 23, 2026 for upgrades.
quote: The program is generally open to participants aged 8 to 70. The Dujiangyan Base of China Conservation and Research Center for the Giant Panda closes from April 23, 2026, to initiate facility upgrades.

claim: The Sichuan Science and Technology Museum on Tianfu Square is free, spans 60,000 sqm with ~600 interactive exhibits over four floors covering space, robotics and physics, best for families.
quote: The Sichuan Science and Technology Museum is free to enter. It covers an area of 60,000 sqm with about 600 exhibits distributed over approximately 20 exhibition halls on four floors.

claim: Jinli is a lantern-lit food and shopping street best visited late afternoon into evening when stalls open and red lanterns light around 7:30 PM in summer.
quote: the ancient alley glows under hundreds of red lanterns (lit daily after sunset, around 7:30 PM in summer/6 PM in winter)

claim: Kuanzhai Xiangzi has free entry across its three Qing-era alleys (Wide for tea, Narrow for boutiques, Well for modern venues), best by 8:30 AM before it becomes a 'human sea' after 11:00 AM.
quote: Kuanzhai Alley transforms into a 'human sea' after 11:00 AM ... Free entry. Individual attractions like Sichuan Opera theaters or museums charge separately.

claim: People's Park functions as Chengdu's communal 'living room' and contains the century-old Heming Teahouse where visitors take gaiwan tea, ear-cleaning, and mahjong, with tea from 16 CNY.
quote: the century-old Heming Teahouse where visitors can enjoy traditional gaiwan tea, get an ear-cleaning treatment ... Tea prices start at 16 CNY

claim: TripAdvisor reviewers regard the People's Park (Renmin/Heming) teahouse as an authentically local spot rather than a tourist trap, with cheap tea (~$2.50) and free refills, though ear-cleaning runs ~100 RMB.
quote: Reviewers position this as an authentically local spot, not a tourist trap ... around $2.50 for tea with complimentary hot water refills ... ear-cleaning services (100 RMB noted as pricey)

claim: Wenshu Monastery, first built in the Sui Dynasty (605-617) with over 1,000 years of history, pairs Zen serenity with a famous Chenlu teahouse and folk-artisan performances.
quote: First built in Sui Dynasty, between 605 ~ 617, Wenshu Monastery has a history over 1000 years ... The teahouse inside Wenshu Monastery is extremely famous

claim: Sino-Ocean Taikoo Li is a free open-air luxury district where ancient rooftops mirror flagship store glass, wrapped around the ticketed Daci Temple (¥30), a 1,600-year-old Buddhist sanctuary best seen early morning.
quote: Taikoo Li: Free ... Daci Temple: ¥30 entrance fee ... the silver-gray tiles of ancient rooftops are mirrored perfectly in the floor-to-ceiling glass of a flagship Gucci store

claim: Dongjiao Memory (Eastern Suburb Memory) is a free, all-day industrial-heritage creative park of red-brick factories, locomotives, galleries, cafes and music venues appealing mainly to young creatives and photographers.
quote: century-old office buildings, red brick factories and locomotives ... Entry Fee: Free admission ... appeals primarily to young creative professionals and photographers

claim: Wangjianglou Park on the south bank of the Jinjiang River features the Chongli Tower, vast bamboo groves, statues and teahouses, warranting 2-3 hours on foot.
quote: situated on the south bank of the Jinjiang River ... celebrated for its exquisite traditional Chinese architecture, particularly the iconic Chongli Tower, and its vast collection of bamboo species ... at least 2 to 3 hours

claim: Hejiang Pavilion sits at the confluence of the Fuhe and Nanhe rivers and anchors a ~15-minute riverside citywalk to the Anshun Covered Bridge.
quote: Hejiang Pavilion is located at the confluence of the Fuhe and Nanhe Rivers ... A citywalk from Hejiang Pavilion to Anshun Covered Bridge takes about 15 minutes

claim: Chengdu-Leshan high-speed trains run from Chengdu East/South stations to Leshan Railway Station in as little as 46 minutes, second-class about CNY 54, with 56 pairs of trains daily.
quote: The quickest journey takes approximately 46 minutes... The ticket costs US$8, equivalent to 54 Chinese yuan (CNY)... 56 pairs of trains operating between Chengdu and Leshan every day.

claim: Leshan Giant Buddha entrance ticket is about CNY 80 per person; an optional boat tour to view the Buddha from the river costs about CNY 70.
quote: The ticket price is 80 yuan per person... the boat fee is 70 CNY if you want to take a boat tour to view the statue from the river.

claim: Sanxingdui Museum is reached via high-speed rail to Guanghan North (then ~15 min taxi) or a direct tourist shuttle from central Chengdu costing CNY 25 in about 1.5 hours; the new hall opened in 2023 to house the new bronze finds.
quote: the fastest way to get from Chengdu to Sanxingdui Museum is by high-speed rail to Guanghan North, then a short taxi ride... about 15 minutes away from the museum by taxi... direct tourist bus from the city center of Chengdu to Sanxingdui... 25 yuan and 1.5 hours

claim: Sanxingdui Museum admission is about CNY 72.
quote: The ticket price is CNY 72.

claim: From Chengdu's Xibu (West) Station, 25-30+ daily bullet trains reach Dujiangyan and Qingchengshan stations in under 30 minutes; Lidui Park station is a 15-minute walk from the Dujiangyan irrigation scenic area.
quote: Xibu Railway Station operates 25+ bullet trains to Dujiangyan Railway Station every day... Lidui Park Station is the closest, dropping you off just a short 15-minute walk from the scenic area's main entrance. The train ride needs less than half an hour.

claim: Dujiangyan Irrigation Park and Mount Qingcheng each cost CNY 80 admission; Sanxingdui Museum is CNY 72.
quote: Dujiangyan Irrigation Park: 80 CNY... Mt. Qingcheng: 80 CNY... Sanxingdui Museum: 72 CNY

claim: Most visitors spend half a day (3-4 hours) at Dujiangyan irrigation system and the remaining half-day at nearby Mount Qingcheng, making both UNESCO sites combinable in one day.
quote: Most visitors spend half a day around 3-4 hours to explore the magical Dujiangyan Irrigation System, and during the rest of that day, they will head to Mount Qingcheng

claim: Huanglongxi Ancient Town is ~40-45 km southeast of Chengdu, reached by direct bus from Xinnanmen Tourist Center every ~20 min (CNY 14) in roughly 70-90 minutes.
quote: Huanglongxi is about 45 km away from Chengdu downtown... scheduled buses every 20 minutes from Chengdu Xinnanmen Tourist Center to Huanglongxi Old Town from 8:00 to 17:30 everyday, with bus tickets costing 14 yuan per person

claim: Xiling Snow Mountain is about 110-117 km from Chengdu in Dayi county, reachable by direct bus in roughly 2.5-3.5 hours, putting it at the edge of a comfortable day trip.
quote: Xiling Snow Mountain is located in Dayi county, Chengdu, about 117 km from Chengdu downtown... easily accessible by bus, taxi and private car within 2.5 hours

claim: Mount Emei is about 170 km from Chengdu, ~1h9m by fastest train but a full day or overnight is needed to do the summit justice, making it impractical to combine with other Chengdu plans on a tight weekend.
quote: Mount Emei is located about 170 km from Chengdu, easily accessible by bus, car, and train within 3 hours... a proven Mount Emei itinerary spans Day 1 for Leshan and Day 2 for Emei

claim: Sichuan pepper (huajiao) produces a tingling, numbing effect from hydroxy-alpha-sanshool, the 'ma' half of mala.
quote: When eaten, Sichuan pepper produces a tingling, numbing effect... due to the presence of hydroxy-alpha sanshool.

claim: Mala combines chili heat and peppercorn numbing; Chengdu's 'mild' baseline is punchier than 'extra spicy' abroad, and a sesame-oil dip coats the stomach; budget hotpot runs CNY 70-90/person.
quote: Chengdu's 'Mild' is a local's baseline... a Wei La pot here is still significantly punchier than an 'Extra Spicy' dish in London or New York... The oil creates a protective coating for your stomach... Budget: CNY 70-90 per person

claim: Popular Chengdu hotpot names include the social-media chain Xiaolongkan, the very busy Bashu Dazhaimen, and herb-broth Yueman Dajiang near Sichuan University.
quote: XiaoLongkan Hot Pot might be the most popular hot pot restaurant among all the locals in Chengdu... Yueman Dajiang... broth cooked with more than 30 kinds of Chinese fragrant herbs.

claim: Signature Chengdu snacks include dan dan noodles, long chao shou (spicy wonton), Zhong's dumplings, san da pao glutinous-rice balls, and brine-stewed spicy rabbit heads.
quote: Long Chao Shou is a kind of Sichuan wonton in spicy flavor... San Da Pao... glutinous rice dough... thick black sugar syrup... Spicy Rabbit Heads... stewing in brine.

claim: Dan dan noodles cost about 12-15 RMB and spicy rabbit heads start around 8 RMB each at spots like Shuangliu Laoma.
quote: you can usually find them for about 12 to 15 RMB... you can find it in restaurants like Shuangliu Laoma and Meiji Rabbit Head starting at 8 RMB per head.

claim: Heming Teahouse in People's Park, founded 1923, is Chengdu's oldest operating teahouse, famous for gaiwan tea, bamboo chairs, mahjong, and ear cleaning (tao er duo), one of the 'Three Great Joys' of Chengdu life.
quote: A visit to Heming Tea House is not complete without experiencing the unique local service of Ear Cleaning (Tao Er Duo), which is considered one of the 'Three Great Joys' of life in Chengdu.

claim: At Heming you order a gaiwan (lidded bowl) experience from 3 RMB up to 18-25 RMB; lid gestures signal refills, a break, or finished, amid mahjong tiles and copper ear-cleaning bells.
quote: you order a Gaiwan (lidded bowl) experience... 3 RMB during morning hours to 18-25 RMB... tilting the lid signals need for refills, placing it on a chair indicates temporary absence, and inverting it inside the bowl signals completion.

claim: Jinli Ancient Street offers heritage snacks in Ming/Qing-style lanes but is tourist-oriented with higher prices, while Kuixinglou Street is the cheaper, more authentic local-frequented alternative.
quote: Jinli Ancient Street is a major tourist attraction... higher prices... Kuixinglou Street is less crowded and offers more budget-friendly snacks, with many local frequented stalls there.

claim: Tourist Sichuan cooking classes typically pair a local wet-market visit with hands-on lessons in dishes like mapo tofu and kung pao chicken.
quote: exploring Liangjiaxiang market... to learn about local spices and ingredients, followed by learning how to make multiple dishes... Mapo Tofu, and Kung Pao Chicken.

claim: Reviewers call the half-day Chengdu cooking class with market visit a trip highlight, authentic and well-organized with knowledgeable instructors.
quote: one of the highlights of their trip to China, perfectly organized, authentic, and full of flavor, with instructors being professional, passionate, and knowledgeable.

claim: Shufeng Yayun Sichuan opera face-changing show runs 1.5 hours starting 8pm daily, tickets 168/198/228 CNY by tier, including free tea and a choice of ear-cleaning, massage or dessert.
quote: Class VIP: 228 ... Class A: 198 ... Class B/C: 168 ... Start Time: 8:00 PM daily ... Duration: 1.5 hours ... Free tea with all tickets; choice of one local experience (ear-cleaning, massage, or dessert)

claim: Shufeng Yayun is a Chengdu opera house at No. 32 Qintai Lu showing Sichuan opera, face-changing, fire-spitting, puppetry, tea art and rolling lantern acts, with bamboo-table tea service included.
quote: the essence of Ba-Shu performing arts, featuring Three Kingdoms culture and Sichuan folk stunts like Sichuan opera, face-changing, fire-spitting, puppetry, tea art, and rolling lantern shows

claim: The Jin (Jinjiang) River night cruise is a roughly 40-minute ride from Dongmen dock past Hejiang Pavilion, Anshun Lang Bridge and Jiuyan Bridge through illuminated light and cultural-projection zones, with peak-weekend waits up to 1.5 hours without advance e-tickets.
quote: 40-minute spellbinding ride ... East Gate Dock (Dongmen), Hejiang Pavilion, Anshun Lang Bridge, and Jiuyan Bridge ... Peak weekend crowds require advance e-ticket purchases to avoid 1.5-hour waits

claim: Jinjiang River night cruise tickets are sold on booking platforms at roughly US$33-38 per person, operating evenings, dropping passengers near Jiuyanqiao Bar Street.
quote: Chengdu: JinJiang River Night Cruise Tickets

claim: Jiuyanqiao ('Nine-Eye Bridge') Bar Street is a riverside stretch of 100+ bars beside the Jin River, lit with neon and red lanterns, ranging from hole-in-the-wall spots to multi-level clubs.
quote: Jiuyanqiao, or "Nine-Eye Bridge," consists of a vibrant stretch of bars running directly alongside the Jin River, beautifully lit up by neon signs and traditional red lanterns

claim: Chengdu is China's rap epicenter (home of Higher Brothers) with a thriving underground scene; Little Bar pioneered it 20 years ago and now runs a 100-cap Yulin punk/rock room and the 800-cap Little Bar Space, alongside NU Space, MAO Livehouse and reggae venue Jah Bar.
quote: the city emerging as China's rap epicenter, home to acts like Higher Brothers ... Little Bar pioneered Chengdu's underground music 20 years ago ... New Little Bar (Yulin): 100-capacity punk/rock venue ... Little Bar Space (MixC mall): 800-capacity warehouse-style venue

claim: A moderate Chengdu night out runs 200-500 RMB per person (beers 20-30 RMB, cocktails 60-100 RMB); Little Bar (4.3/5) on Fangqin St is the headline indie venue, with Jiuyanqiao (4.1/5) and Lan Kwai Fong (4.4/5) as the main bar districts.
quote: A moderate night out ranges from 200-500 RMB per person, with local beers around 20-30 RMB and cocktails at 60-100 RMB ... Little Bar (4.3/5 stars) ... Jiuyanqiao Bar Street (4.1/5 stars) ... Chengdu Lan Kwai Fong (4.4/5 stars)

claim: Chengdu's Lan Kwai Fong is a polished entertainment complex modeled on Hong Kong's district, packed with mega-clubs and cocktail lounges including Space Club and Playhouse focused on EDM and bottle service.
quote: Chengdu's Lan Kwai Fong is a polished entertainment complex that was meticulously modeled after the original Hong Kong district ... The undisputed heavy hitters of the area are Space Club and Playhouse, both providing massive, immersive EDM environments

claim: Taikoo Li Chengdu is a free, open-plan low-rise heritage shopping district (rated 4.4/5, ~2-3 hours, open to 22:00, 22:30 weekends) next to Chunxi Road, popular for night people-watching and social-media photos, with the Daci Temple inside.
quote: Free to visit ... Rating: 4.4 of 5 bubbles ... Hours: 10:00 AM-10:00 PM daily (extended to 10:30 PM Friday-Sunday) ... Suggested Duration: 2-3 hours ... popular with social media content creators, particularly at night

claim: The IFS panda sculpture is a giant climbing-panda public artwork on the exterior of IFS mall at Taikoo Li, free to view at any time and a top night photo spot.
quote: An iconic, larger-than-life panda sculpture artfully climbing the side of the IFS Mall ... free to view and photograph. The panda sculpture is visible at all times

claim: China's visa-free transit was extended to 240 hours (10 days) effective December 17 2024 for 54 eligible countries, allowing cross-province travel across 24 regions, replacing the old 72/144-hour policy.
quote: for no more than 240 hours ... individuals from 54 eligible countries, including Russia, Brazil, the United Kingdom, the United States of America, and Canada ... can make cross-province travels within the allowed areas ... in these 24 provinces

claim: Under the visa-free transit policy travelers must hold an onward ticket to a third country; entering without continuing to a third destination is treated as illegal entry, and Chengdu Tianfu airport is an eligible port.
quote: You must be going on to a third country after leaving China—entering under the visa-free transit policy when not continuing travel to a third country will be considered illegal entry.

claim: Foreigners can link international Visa/Mastercard to Alipay and WeChat Pay without a Chinese bank account or phone number, but should set up both apps, carry RMB cash, bring two physical cards, and test everything before traveling.
quote: the best way to pay in China as a foreigner is to set up Alipay first, set up WeChat Pay second, carry RMB cash, bring two physical bank cards, and test everything before your first full day of travel.

claim: Since late 2025 Alipay and WeChat Pay apply stricter verification when binding foreign cards, with checks taking 24-72 hours or failing outright, while verified foreign users now have a per-transaction limit around $5,000 USD.
quote: Since late 2025, both Alipay and WeChat Pay began implementing stricter verification protocols for foreign card binding ... can take 24-72 hours—or fail entirely

claim: The best time to visit Chengdu is spring (March-June) and autumn (September-November), with April and October offering comfortable 15-22C temperatures and the most active pandas; summer is hot/humid (often 35C) and winter is a damp 0-10C cold.
quote: the best travel time to visit Chengdu is from March to June and September to November ... Visit in April or October. These months offer the most comfortable temperatures (avg. 15°C to 22°C)

claim: Visitors should avoid Chinese national holidays — especially National Day Golden Week (October 1-7), May Day (May 1-5) and Lunar New Year — and in 2026 the Mid-Autumn Festival (Sept 25-27) runs into Golden Week creating extreme crowds; pandas are most active before 9:30 AM.
quote: In 2026, the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday (September 25-27) is very close to the National Day "Golden Week" (October 1–7), which will be the busiest travel week in the world. Unless you love massive crowds, do not visit during this time.

claim: Tianfu Airport (TFU) is ~50-60 km from downtown with Metro Line 18 express reaching South Railway Station in ~33-35 min for 10 CNY, while a DiDi/taxi runs 35-60 min and costs roughly 180-320 CNY; Shuangliu (CTU) is only ~16 km out with Line 10 reaching Tianfu Square in 35-45 min.
quote: An express metro line runs between Tianfu Airport and South Railway Station, taking only 33 minutes ... A trip to central Tianfu City Center usually costs 180–260 CNY during the day

claim: The Tianfu Airport express metro runs hourly from 6am to 11pm reaching South Railway Station in 33 minutes, while regular Line 18 runs every 8 minutes taking about 50 minutes over 8 stops.
quote: an express line operates from 6 am to 11 pm with service every hour, taking only 33 minutes to reach South Railway Station. The regular Line 18 runs more frequently (every 8 minutes) but requires about 50 minutes with 8 stops.

claim: Foreigners ride the Chengdu metro most easily by activating the Alipay transport QR code (set city to Chengdu) and scanning at turnstiles with a linked international card; a physical Tianfu Tong card (~25 CNY) suits longer stays and is sold at major stations like Tianfu Square and Chunxi Road.
quote: The easiest way is using the Alipay app. Select "Transport," change the location to Chengdu, and activate the metro QR code. You can scan this code directly at the turnstiles

claim: DiDi ride-hailing can be used directly inside WeChat as a built-in mini-program with no separate app or Chinese phone number, with an English interface and auto-translated driver messages, once a foreign card is linked to WeChat Pay.
quote: You can use DiDi directly from WeChat as a built-in mini program with no separate app and no Chinese phone number needed ... The interface is in English, and driver messages come through auto-translated both ways.

claim: For first-timers the best base is Chunxi Road / Taikoo Li — central, with intersecting Metro Lines 2 and 3, abundant food, international-friendly hotels and walkable landmarks — while Tianfu Square is a less scenic but highly practical alternative for a 2-3 day visit.
quote: Chunxi Road and Taikoo Li give you the easiest mix of metro access, food, international-friendly hotels, shopping, and late-night energy ... Tianfu Square is not the prettiest area ... but it is one of the most practical

claim: A workable 2-day shape pairs Kuanzhai (Wide & Narrow) Alley, Wuhou Temple and Jinli Ancient Street (best at lantern-lighting ~7pm) on day one with an early-morning Chengdu Panda Base visit (pandas most active 8:30-9:00 feeding) on day two, leaving evenings free for a fine-dining dinner.
quote: Start your first day at 9:00 AM in the charming Kuanzhai Alley ... take Metro Line 4 to Wuhou Temple ... Jinli Ancient Street. The best time to visit is right when the lanterns light up (around 7:00 PM ... head to Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding. The giant pandas are more active at 08:30 - 09:00
